target.title: refactor(tts): consolidate config merge
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Core TTS config resolution and the voice-call plugin carried separate copies of the same deep-merge contract. Keeping both implementations made TTS override semantics and prototype-pollution hardening vulnerable to drift.

The broader deep-merge audit found no other compatible group: include merging, settings layering, CLI merging, migrations, Codex thread config, runtime merge patches, QA patches, and test helpers each have distinct array, `undefined`, cloning, deletion, error, or ownership policies.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the exact shared TTS behavior into a narrow `src/tts` helper and exposes it to the voice-call plugin through the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/speech-core` boundary. It preserves the established contract: nested record merge, array/scalar replacement, ignored `undefined` overrides, and blocked prototype-mutation keys.

No generic merge API or new dependency is introduced, and all non-compatible merge implementations remain with their current owners.

## User Impact

No intentional behavior change. Core, agent, channel, account, voice-call, and telephony TTS overrides continue to resolve as before, with one canonical implementation reducing future drift risk.

## Evidence

- Delegated Blacksmith Testbox: `tbx_01kwncvdra419h5pv816sajnkz` (`blacksmith-testbox`, exit 0)
- Focused tests: 53 passed across the new merge contract, speech-core TTS, and voice-call telephony TTS suites
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed core/extensions typechecks, lint, import-cycle, duplicate, dependency, database-first, and remaining changed gates
- Formatting check: passed for all touched source/test files
- Autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings (0.98 correctness confidence)
- Production code: net -22 lines
